subject: One possible suggestion on improvement of plotAllometry

messages.author: 767ec98223db0a64
messages.subject: One possible suggestion on improvement of plotAllometry
parts:
Dear Prof. Adams and Dr. Michael,

In current version of geomorph and RRPP, the logsz argument in plotAllometry could be set regardless of whether the formula for the associated lm.rrpp object included original or log CS. 

An example is as follows:

library(geomorph)

data("larvalMorph")

Y.gpa <- gpagen(larvalMorph$tailcoords, curves = larvalMorph$tail.sliders,
                ProcD = FALSE, print.progress = FALSE)

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(Y.gpa, treatment = larvalMorph$treatment,
                           family = larvalMorph$family) 

fit1 <- procD.lm(coords ~ Csize,
                 data = gdf, print.progress = FALSE) # simple allometry model

a <- plotAllometry(fit1, size = gdf$Csize, logsz = F, method = "RegScore")
a1 <- a$RegScore

b <- plotAllometry(fit1, size = gdf$Csize, logsz = T, method = "RegScore")
b1 <- b$RegScore

fit2 <- procD.lm(coords ~ log(Csize), data = gdf, print.progress = FALSE)
c <- plotAllometry(fit2, size = gdf$Csize, logsz = F, method = "RegScore")
c1 <- c$RegScore

d <- plotAllometry(fit2, size = gdf$Csize, logsz = T, method = "RegScore")
d1 <- d$RegScore

I think only shape scores from a1 and d1 are sensible. If this is the case, would it be preferrable to constrain the argument for logsz to be consistent with the formula in lm.rrpp fit object?

Best regards,
Patrick Wen

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] One possible suggestion on improvement of plotAllometry
parts:
You are correct that it can be set regardless of what the user put into the model. It is up to the user to be sensible and consistent between their model and their plots of it. As with all R-packages, geomorph simply provides common options for users to select based upon their circumstances.

 

Dean

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] One possible suggestion on improvement of plotAllometry
parts:
Patrick, 

What you deem sensible might not comport with another’s perspective.  For example, one might perform an analysis that has centroid size of landmark configurations associated with the head in the linear model with perhaps some other variables, and might wish to entertain whether estimates made from that linear model have an association with body size.  There is no explicit expectation that the size variable in plotAllometry has to also be part of the linear model formula for the fit that was performed.  What is sensible to me is that this function is not overly prohibitive.  Concerning the suggestion you make I do not agree it would improve the function.  It would only limit its use to certain models..

Mike
